title: API Versioning, Pagination and HTTP Caching
summary: Quick revision notes on choosing a versioning scheme, keeping APIs backward compatible, paginating with offset vs cursor, and caching with ETag and Cache-Control.

chapters.title: API Design Mental Model
points: Versioning, pagination and caching all protect clients: the contract must stay stable while data and servers change
Version = a named contract; bump it only for breaking changes, never for additive ones
Pagination = return a bounded slice plus a way to ask for the next slice
Caching = reuse a stored response while fresh, or revalidate cheaply when stale
Core request flow: client sends version + page position + validators; server returns data + next position + cache headers

chapters.title: URL vs Header Versioning
points: URL versioning: /v1/users; visible, easy to route, curl and cache; but the URL (resource identity) changes per version
Header versioning: Accept: application/vnd.example+json; version=2 or X-API-Version: 2; clean URLs, but hidden and harder to test in a browser
Header-based responses must send Vary: Accept (or the version header) or shared caches serve the wrong version
Comparison: URL = simple and discoverable; header = purist REST, better for long-lived APIs; query param (?v=2) is easy but pollutes cache keys
Mistake: versioning every endpoint separately or bumping the major version for small changes; choose one scheme and version the whole API

chapters.title: Backward Compatibility Rules
points: Safe (non-breaking): add optional fields, add new endpoints, add optional query params, add enum values only if clients tolerate unknowns
Breaking: remove or rename a field, change a type, make an optional param required, change status codes or error shapes, change semantics
Tolerant reader: clients ignore unknown fields; servers accept unknown optional input; this makes additive change safe
Deprecation flow: announce, add Deprecation and Sunset headers, monitor usage per version, then remove after the sunset date
Example: rename user_name to username by returning both fields for a transition period, then drop the old one in the next version

chapters.title: Offset vs Cursor Pagination
points: Offset: ?limit=20&offset=40 maps to SQL LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40; supports jump-to-page and totals
Offset problems: the DB scans and discards skipped rows (slow on deep pages), and inserts or deletes between requests cause duplicate or missing items
Cursor (keyset): ?limit=20&after=<opaque token>; SQL WHERE (created_at, id) < (:c, :i) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20; uses an index, stays fast at any depth
Cursor needs a unique, stable sort key (add id as a tiebreaker); return an opaque encoded cursor plus next_cursor, and null at the end
Comparison: offset = simple, random access, unstable on changing data; cursor = fast, consistent, only next/prev, no total page count; use cursor for feeds and large or fast-changing data

chapters.title: Caching with ETag and Cache-Control
points: Cache-Control: max-age=N (fresh for N seconds), s-maxage (shared caches only), no-cache (store but must revalidate), no-store (never store), private vs public
ETag: a validator, the version fingerprint of a representation; the server sends ETag: "abc123"
Conditional request: the client sends If-None-Match: "abc123"; if unchanged, server returns 304 Not Modified with no body, saving bandwidth
Writes: If-Match: <etag> on PUT/PATCH gives optimistic concurrency; a mismatch returns 412 Precondition Failed

Mistakes: no-cache is not no-store; caching personalised responses as public; missing Vary on varying responses; ETag differing across servers behind a load balancer; setting max-age on data that changes

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet
points: Versioning: URL /v1/ = simple; header + Vary = clean URLs; bump the major version only for breaking changes
Breaking vs safe: add = safe; remove, rename, retype or make required = breaking; deprecate via Sunset header
Pagination: offset = LIMIT/OFFSET, jumpable, slow and unstable; cursor = keyset WHERE, fast and stable, opaque token
Cache-Control: max-age, s-maxage, no-cache (revalidate), no-store (never), public vs private; add Vary for varying responses
ETag flow: ETag out, If-None-Match in, 304 back; If-Match on writes, 412 on mismatch
